title: Comparison of locally closed extension generators along the pro-étale comparison
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]) and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaves with value $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and on the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and for a scheme $T$ the comparison morphism $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ with its inverse image $\nu_T^*$ on module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ be a locally closed immersion, $C$ its scheme-theoretic closure [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], $j:S\hookrightarrow C$ the resulting open immersion [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image; def-weil-open-immersion] and $g:C\hookrightarrow X$ the closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $a=g\circ j$. On the étale sites $j_!$ is the extension by zero of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and $g_*$ the direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; on the pro-étale sites $j_!$ is the extension by zero of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero] and $g_*$ the direct image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then:

1. On either site $g_*$ is an exact functor of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules; consequently, for every sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $S$ (on the same site), the canonical map $(g_*j_!M)[0]\to Rg_*(j_!M[0])$ to the right derived direct image is an isomorphism in $D(X,\Lambda)$.
2. Let $L$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ that is locally constant with finite projective $\Lambda$-module stalks at all geometric points [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves; def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Then $\nu_S^*L$ is locally constant on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf], and its stalk at every geometric point of $S$ [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] is a finite projective, in particular flat, $\Lambda$-module.
3. For every sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ there is an isomorphism $\nu_X^*(g_*j_!M)\cong g_*j_!(\nu_S^*M)$ of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, natural in $M$, where the left side uses the étale functors and the right side the pro-étale functors.

The empty stratum and the zero ring are allowed; no separatedness of $X$ is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover of $X$ by spectra of Noetherian rings: local Noetherianity supplies the cover and quasi-compactness supplies a finite subcover. Each member has Noetherian underlying space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space], so [lem-kun-finite-union-noetherian] makes $|X|$ Noetherian. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], every subset of $|X|$ is quasi-compact. In particular the complementary open $V=X\setminus g(C)$ is quasi-compact, and $V\cap W$ is quasi-compact for every open $W\subseteq X$. This supplies the quasi-compact complementary open required by the pro-étale open–closed lemma, without assuming that $X$ is separated.

source.place: Tags 0053 (lemma-finite-union-Noetherian), 04ZA (lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact); affine Noetherian topology: algebra.tex Tag 00FQ (lemma-Noetherian-topology)

proof.text: For the closed immersion $g:C\hookrightarrow X$ and its complementary open $V$, [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] explicitly states that the étale module direct image $g_*$ is exact. For the pro-étale site apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with $A=\underline\Lambda_X$ and complementary open $V$. Its hypothesis on the open holds by Step 1, and it explicitly states exactness of $g_*$. The canonical ring isomorphism $g^{-1}\underline\Lambda_X\cong\underline\Lambda_C$ of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] identifies its coefficients with the constant coefficients of this item. Under this identification the direct image action is the one induced by constant scalar sections, hence the $g_*$ specified in the statement. This proves exactness on both sites.

proof.text: An exact functor has the termwise derived factorization of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] says that its canonical comparison to its right derived functor is invertible for every complex. On each site apply these statements to the exact functor $g_*$ of Step 2 and the complex $K=(j_!M)[0]$. Termwise application gives $C(g_*)K=(g_*j_!M)[0]$. Thus the particular canonical map $(g_*j_!M)[0]\longrightarrow Rg_*(j_!M[0])$ is an isomorphism, proving clause 1. No acyclicity or constructibility hypothesis on $M$ is used.

Each stalk $L_{\bar s}$ is finitely generated over the finite ring $\Lambda$. A finite set of $r$ generators gives a surjection of sets $\Lambda^r\twoheadrightarrow L_{\bar s}$, so that stalk is finite as a set. Thus $L$ is lisse in the precise sense of [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin]. Part (a) of that lemma implies that $\nu_S^*L$ is locally constant on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (and has finite stalks). This uses only the forward implication of that lemma.

For every geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$, [lem-cbc-proetale-comparison-stalk] gives a $\Lambda$-linear isomorphism $(\nu_S^*L)_{\bar s}\cong L_{\bar s}$, not merely a bijection of the underlying sets. The right side is finite projective by hypothesis, so the left side is finite projective too: transport a finite generating set and a splitting of a finite free surjection across this isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat] it is flat. Together with Step 4 this proves clause 2. No assertion that geometric stalks detect arbitrary pro-étale sheaf isomorphisms is needed.

proof.text: Identify the pro-étale extension-by-zero conventions. The item's pro-étale $j_!$, the sheafified left Kan extension, is taken with values in $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda$. By [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves], applied to $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and to $C_{\mathrm{proet}}$, restriction of scalars along the constant-ring unit $\iota$ is an equivalence from sheaves of $\underline\Lambda$-modules to sheaves valued in $\Lambda$-modules, keeping the underlying abelian sheaves and their maps; so this $j_!$ is a functor between the module categories of the item, and restriction of sections commutes with these identifications. The left-Kan-extension definition has the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction], whose $j^*$ is isomorphic to restriction, $(j^*G)(T\to S)\cong G(T\to S\to C)$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], the open immersion $j:S\hookrightarrow C$ identifies $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $C_{\mathrm{proet}}/S$, including the topology, the restriction functor, and the restricted constant coefficient ring $\Lambda_C|_S\cong\Lambda_S$ (identity on constant sections, so compatible with $\iota$). In this presentation [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] says that the sheafified extension-by-zero presheaf, which is the definition used by the open comparison lemma, is left adjoint to the same restriction. Taking for $\delta$ that isomorphism of the two right adjoints, [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] gives a natural isomorphism between these two left adjoints, compatible with their units. This identifies the pro-étale $j_!$ used below with the convention in the item, without any extra hypothesis on $j$.

proof.text: The affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] says that $g$ is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], an affine morphism is quasi-compact and separated, in particular quasi-separated. Hence $g$ satisfies both morphism hypotheses of comparison of derived direct images. These are properties of $g$; separatedness of $X$ over a base is not required.

Put $N=j^{\mathrm{et}}_!M$. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] to $g$ and $N[0]\in D^+(C_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, using Step 7. It gives, naturally in $N$, an isomorphism $
u_X^*Rg^{\mathrm{et}}_*(N[0])\cong Rg^{\mathrm{proet}}_*
u_C^*(N[0])$. On both sides the exactness established in Step 2 identifies $Rg_*$ with termwise $g_*$ by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Also [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] says that comparison pullback is exact, is computed termwise, and commutes with cohomology. Both sides are therefore represented by single complexes, with degree-zero objects $
u_X^*(g^{\mathrm{et}}_*N)$ and $g^{\mathrm{proet}}_*(
u_C^*N)$. Apply $\mathcal H^0$ to obtain a natural sheaf isomorphism $ eta_N:
u_X^*g^{\mathrm{et}}_*N\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{\mathrm{proet}}_*
u_C^*N$. Here $\mathcal H^0(H[0])=H$ follows directly from the single-complex differential being zero. This argument uses a derived comparison only on bounded-below complexes, exactly its stated domain.

proof.text:
By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] for the open immersion $j:S\hookrightarrow C$, there is a natural sheaf isomorphism $\alpha_M:
u_C^*j^{\mathrm{et}}_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!
u_S^*M$. Step 6 identifies its pro-étale $j_!$ with the convention in the item. Compose $ eta_{j^{\mathrm{et}}_!M}$ of Step 8 with $g^{\mathrm{proet}}_*(\alpha_M)$ to obtain $
u_X^*(g^{\mathrm{et}}_*j^{\mathrm{et}}_!M)\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{\mathrm{proet}}_*j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!(
u_S^*M)$, which proves clause 3. Each factor is natural in $M$, so the composite is natural as well. Every argument also applies when $S$ is empty or $\Lambda$ is the zero ring: the relevant module sheaves on the empty site, or over the zero ring, are zero, and all displayed maps are then the unique isomorphisms between zero objects.

tool_uses.why: Noetherian affine topology is a generic topological input for checking the quasi-compact complement required by the unit’s exact closed direct image.
The finite affine cover argument assembles Noetherian topology, without changing the flat-model route.
Quasi-compactness of the complementary open checks the pro-etale exactness hypothesis.
Its statement explicitly gives exactness of etale closed-immersion module direct image, as required by the complement of the unit proof.
Its module exactness and extension-by-zero adjunction supply the corresponding pro-etale open/closed tools.
It identifies the inverse-image constant rings and scalar conventions in the module open/closed lemma.
The abstract exact-functor lemma identifies the specified canonical map to Rg_*; the unit uses Rg_*=g_*.
Its forward implication supplies local constancy after comparison pullback, as the unit’s first paragraph requires.
The linear stalk comparison transports finite projectivity without assuming conservativity of geometric pro-etale stalks.
Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the two existing extension-by-zero presentations.
Its qcqs direct-image comparison is specialized to the closed immersion and degree-zero sheaves.
Exact comparison pullback makes the degree-zero specialization valid and natural.
The open-extension comparison is composed with the closed direct-image comparison to transport the unit’s generators.
It identifies open subscheme restriction and its constant coefficient rings with the localized ringed-site restriction, to compare the two existing j_! definitions.
Its statement identifies the actual sheafified extension-by-zero presheaf as a left adjoint to restriction, so uniqueness applies to the two j_! conventions.
